FIELD REFERENCE

White sturgeon: identification, size and trip rules

White sturgeon (Acipenser transmontanus) are large Pacific-coast fish with five rows of bony plates, a blunt snout and four barbels nearer the snout tip than the mouth. Do not identify them by size alone. Before a trip, check the exact river, season and release rules: nearby sturgeon fisheries can have different restrictions.

Compare green sturgeon, then check the Fraser River catch-and-release trip and British Columbia licence.

Updated 2026-11-23 · Castward

How do you identify a white sturgeon?

Key factDetail
Scientific nameAcipenser transmontanus
White sturgeonBlunt snout; barbels nearer the snout tip than the mouth
Green sturgeonBarbels nearer the mouth; do not rely on colour alone
Size referenceOregon Sea Grant: up to 20 ft (6 m) and over 1,500 lb (680 kg); not a likely catch size
RangePacific coast, southern Alaska to Baja California; mainly freshwater, with some marine use
CaliforniaCatch and release only; report-card season October 1–June 30
California report deadlineJuly 31 after the report card expires
IdahoNo harvest; record fish must be measured in the water

White or green sturgeon: which features matter?

Start with the head and barbels, then compare the bony plates. White sturgeon have barbels nearer the snout tip; green sturgeon have them nearer the mouth. California lists at least 36 lateral plates for white sturgeon and 33 or fewer for green sturgeon. A single colour or size clue is not enough.

Read the source

When can you plan a California white sturgeon trip?

California’s report-card season runs from October 1 through June 30, and white sturgeon fishing is catch and release only. Carry the card while fishing. Return it, or report online, by July 31 after it expires. Check the current water-specific regulations before travel; a card does not open a closed water.

Read the source

Can you keep a white sturgeon in Oregon?

Do not assume that a general species page gives permission to keep a fish. Oregon directs anglers to the regulations for each water and season. Green sturgeon cannot be targeted there, even for catch and release. Release an accidentally caught green sturgeon immediately and unharmed.

Read the source

How should you measure a white sturgeon in Idaho?

Idaho requires white sturgeon entered for a record to stay in the water for measurement. Its instructions use the belly side, from the snout to the tip of the upper tail lobe. Prepare the tape and photographs first, reduce handling time and release the fish promptly. Idaho does not allow white sturgeon harvest.

Read the source

Do white sturgeon live only in rivers?

No. Fisheries and Oceans Canada describes white sturgeon as mainly freshwater fish that can also enter Pacific coastal waters. Its guide names the Fraser estuary and nearby straits. That range describes where the species occurs; it does not establish an open fishery or a public launch for your trip.

Read the source

What should you know about white sturgeon?

Is white sturgeon the same as green sturgeon?

No. They are different species. Compare the barbels and bony plates before you apply the rules.

How big can white sturgeon grow?

Oregon Sea Grant gives an upper size reference of 20 ft (6 m) and over 1,500 lb (680 kg).

Can you tell a sturgeon’s age from its length?

Length alone does not establish an individual fish’s age. Do not assign an age to a catch from a photograph or tape measurement.

Do California anglers need a report card for released fish?

Yes. Carry a Sturgeon Fishing Report Card while targeting white sturgeon, even though the fishery is catch and release only.

Can you target green sturgeon in Oregon?

No. Oregon prohibits targeting green sturgeon for retention or catch and release.

Can an Idaho white sturgeon qualify for a weight record?

No. Idaho allows no white sturgeon harvest and accepts the species only in its catch-and-release record category.
